metadata.title: Enphase Shares Tumble as Quarterly Earnings Fall Short of Expectations

content.text:
Shares of Enphase Energy (NASDAQ: ENPH) plunged approximately 16% in early Wednesday trading after the U.S. solar technology company reported disappointing third-quarter earnings and issued a significantly weaker-than-expected revenue outlook for the final quarter of 2026.
According to the company's earnings release, third-quarter revenue reached $293.3 million, down 28.5% from $410.4 million a year earlier and below Wall Street expectations of $303.85 million.
Adjusted earnings per share fell to $0.41, missing analyst estimates of $0.51 and declining from $0.90 in the same quarter last year. GAAP net income dropped to $23.4 million from $66.6 million.
Enphase also reported a non-GAAP gross margin of 45%, compared with 49.2% a year earlier.
The company's fourth-quarter outlook delivered another blow to investors. Enphase expects revenue of $225 million to $255 million, substantially below analysts' consensus estimate of approximately $300.5 million.
Weak demand for residential solar installations continues to weigh on the company, particularly in the United States, where higher borrowing costs and the expiration of the Section 25D federal tax credit have dampened consumer interest.
U.S. product sell-through declined 35% year-over-year, while European sell-through fell 12% sequentially, reflecting seasonal weakness and slowing demand, particularly in France.
Enphase shipped 1.42 million microinverters and 129.9 megawatt-hours of batteries during the quarter.
Despite the downturn, the company is pursuing new opportunities in commercial solar, battery storage and AI data center power infrastructure.
Enphase recently demonstrated its solid-state transformer technology and expects commercial shipments for AI data centers to begin in 2028.
